task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: opponent next-possession points per possession (PPP) after play type X
AVOID labels defined from play-type PPP differences
own-sequence lagged effects of play types
derived play-type possession records built from play-by-play
sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock
methodological_questions: Is the opponent next-possession PPP difference after play X large enough to justify an AVOID label, and what threshold defines 'large enough'?
Are play-type labels valid enough to carry PPP differences, given foul leakage and low initiation_type coverage?
Does defining AVOID from the same next-possession PPP outcome that is being tested make the label circular?
How should own-sequence lag effects be estimated while controlling for score state, opponent quality, and lineup?
Do pooled effects hold at team level, where cells are small?

historical_evidence.finding: Record states an observed hypothesis that after the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above Y's unconditional H2 baseline, with a defensive aftershock for every play type. The recorded result reports that the aftershock replicated for 8/8 play types in all games and in playoffs (for example CUT +0.119 n=21,398 all-games and +0.131 n=1,145 playoffs; TRANSITION +0.135 n=26,262 all-games). Top pair premiums cited include PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084 n=565. Scope annotation: two records on sequential play-type pairs (458,604 opponent possessions); team-level cells include tiny n. Limitation recorded as [prior work]. [prior work] text is truncated in the retrieval output, and I did not read the full family record.

Play-type labeling audit found that 36% of OTHER possessions end in fouls, inflating OTHER PPP; DRIVE sits 12 points below the foul benchmark; PNR shows a 22% foul rate; initiation_type maps only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a play type. Recorded verdict: artifact_found. Validation status: no_validation_recorded (evidence NOT_RECORDED). Scope annotation: applies to analyses whose result depends on PPP differences between play types, especially OTHER and DRIVE, or on initiation_type; does not record label error for other categories or the bias in any downstream estimate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type PPP differences and the initiation_type mapping as the basis for play-type labels and for interpreting play-type efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact: OTHER PPP is inflated by foul endings (36%), DRIVE is 12 points below the foul benchmark, PNR has a 22% foul rate, and initiation_type covers only 0.7% of possessions. Any AVOID label built on these PPP differences would inherit the artifact. No validation was recorded.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project recorded a defensive aftershock pattern (the next offensive play type scores above baseline after a play type) across all 8 play types, replicated in all games and playoffs, in the [prior work] family. This is a related but not identical result to the question.

Earlier work recorded that play-type PPP differences are contaminated by foul-ending possessions and that the initiation_type mapping covers under 1% of possessions. Any AVOID label that depends on play-type PPP must first pass a label-validity check.
evidence_does_not_establish: Does not establish any AVOID label definition, threshold, or classification rule. The retrieved records do not define AVOID.

Does not establish the size of the opponent next-possession PPP effect after play X in a form that drives AVOID labels. [prior work] reports aftershock PPP-related quantities, but the retrieved text does not give the exact estimand or the threshold used.
Does not establish own-sequence lag effects separately from the opponent aftershock, since the retrieved hypothesis wording is ambiguous about whose possession follows.

Does not establish label validity for categories other than OTHER and DRIVE, and does not quantify bias in any downstream estimate (SF-[prior work] scope annotation). [prior work] text for [prior work] is truncated in retrieval.
Does not establish stability in 2025-26 data, which is partial at the 2026-06-19 date.
own_inferences: The AVOID question is partly circular if AVOID is defined from the same next-possession PPP outcome that is being tested. The label and the test outcome must be separated, for example by estimating the threshold on one season and testing on another.

The foul-leakage finding bears directly on the question because AVOID-type labels are usually built from PPP. Foul-ending possessions should be excluded or modelled before any play-type PPP comparison.
Team-level AVOID decisions are likely underpowered because the [prior work] team-level cells are tiny. Pooled league-level estimates may be stable, but team-level labels would be noisy.
The own-sequence lag question is separable from the opponent-aftershock question only if the possession order and team attribution are checked directly in the play-by-play data.
uncertainties: The AVOID threshold and its meaning ('large enough') are not defined in the task or in any retrieved record.
The full text of FAM:[prior work] was not read; its truncated outcome and top pair premium figures are reported only as shown.
Whether SF-[prior work]'s 0.7% initiation_type coverage has been fixed since it was recorded is unknown.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13 and the 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-06-19, so the usable data window at the question date is uncertain.
Possession-level sample size and per-play-type counts for the question's X are not given; power has not been computed.
Historical record statuses are as recorded and may not reflect a formal hypothesis test.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the retrieved records, the plan would have been to test the opponent next-possession PPP effect directly from the play-by-play. The SF-[prior work] artifact record shows that play-type PPP differences are contaminated by foul endings and that the initiation_type mapping is nearly empty, so an AVOID label built on those PPP differences would be unreliable. The decision therefore changes from a straightforward test to proceeding only after label validation. The [prior work] record supports the plausibility of a next-possession aftershock but was not treated as a confirmation of AVOID labels, because it does not define AVOID and carries a small-sample limitation.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels have foul leakage (36% of OTHER possessions end in fouls; DRIVE 12 points below the foul benchmark; PNR 22% foul rate) and initiation_type covers only 0.7% of possessions. Labels must be validated before PPP differences are interpreted.
If AVOID is defined from the same next-possession PPP being tested, the label and outcome are circular. A separate threshold-setting sample is needed.
Team-level cells are tiny ([prior work] scope annotation). AVOID labels at team level would be underpowered without pooling or hierarchical modelling.

prior_work.summary: [prior work] reports a defensive aftershock and sequential pair premium across all 8 play types, replicated in playoffs, but it does not define an AVOID label and its scope is limited by small team-level cells. SF-[prior work] is an artifact record showing foul leakage and near-empty initiation_type mapping in play-type PPP, which bears directly on any label built from PPP. Neither record answers the AVOID-threshold question or the own-sequence lag question as posed.

risks.text: Foul-ending possessions inflate OTHER PPP and bias DRIVE and PNR. Play-type labels are unvalidated (no_validation_recorded) and initiation_type covers 0.7% of possessions.
AVOID labels defined from the outcome being tested are circular; threshold and test must use separate data.
Opponent quality, score margin, garbage-time possessions, period, and lineup or matchup composition may drive next-possession PPP independently of play X.
Team-level cells are small; the [prior work] record flags small samples. Power for own-sequence lags after restricting to validated possessions has not been computed.
Testing 8 play types across several lags and both opponent and own sequences inflates false positives unless corrected.
Play-type classification from play-by-play action and sub-type fields may be noisy; reliability is not recorded.
Aftershock-type effects can appear in placebo or shuffled sequences if base rates or period structure differ; a placebo must be defined before analysis.
Scoring environment changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26; 2025-26 data is partial at the question date.
Large PPP differences can arise from low base rates of some play types; the AVOID threshold must be set relative to baseline frequency.

design.estimand: Difference in opponent next-possession PPP after a validated opponent play type X versus that play type's unconditional baseline, with a separate own-sequence lag estimate; AVOID is a pre-specified threshold on this difference with the lower confidence bound above the threshold.
design.unit: Possession pair: a classified opponent possession followed by the next possession by the same team (opponent next-possession PPP). Foul-ending possessions excluded from the primary analysis; a sensitivity analysis models them.
design.sample: Complete seasons only: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season only from 2026-04-13 onward; 2025-26 playoffs excluded at the 2026-06-19 date because they are partial. Label-validation sample drawn from 2022-23 and 2023-24; threshold and test from 2024-25 and later (or a held-out season split).
design.power: Not yet computed. Before analysis, compute per-play-type possession counts after foul exclusion and the minimum detectable PPP difference at 80% power with game-clustered variance. Team-level AVOID labels are not planned unless power is shown adequate; otherwise use pooled league-level estimates with hierarchical shrinkage.
design.controls: Score margin, period, garbage-time flag, opponent and team strength (prior-season net rating), lineup or matchup minutes from the matchup and rotation files, and possession-order checks. Own-sequence lag and opponent aftershock estimated in the same model with a shared baseline.
design.falsification: Placebo tests: (a) shuffled possession order within game; (b) the same statistic computed for play types that should not precede the outcome; (c) a pre-possession placebo window. The effect must exceed placebo effects to count as supported.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across play types and lags; a pre-registered primary contrast set. Exploratory results are labelled as such.
design.decision_rule: Gate 1: label validation must show foul leakage below a pre-set tolerance and initiation_type or alternative classification coverage above a pre-set threshold, otherwise stop and report artifact. Gate 2: AVOID applied only if the lower 95% bound on the next-possession PPP difference exceeds the pre-registered threshold in the held-out season and placebo effects are below threshold. Otherwise report uncertain or rejected.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, matchup minutes, box-score summary, and the derived play-type possession graph database; versions frozen at 2026-06-19 with the complete-season cut-offs stated in the sample field.
